corpus-0001.label: benign
corpus-0001.reason: Untargeted internet-wide scanning against a single exposed port. No authentication attempt, no follow-on activity.

corpus-0002.label: benign
corpus-0002.reason: Long-lived read-only service account performing its routine inventory sweep. Threat-list hit is a stale shared-hosting entry.

corpus-0003.label: malicious
corpus-0003.reason: Interactive developer credentials used via Tor at 3am. No business reason for anonymised access; consistent with stolen key usage.

corpus-0004.label: benign
corpus-0004.reason: Routine background scanning. Instance sits behind a security group that denies the probed ports.

corpus-0005.label: benign
corpus-0005.reason: CI runner calls GetCallerIdentity on every pipeline start. Source is the build vendor's shared egress range, which carries a stale listing.

corpus-0006.label: malicious
corpus-0006.reason: Bulk secret retrieval at 2am from an unfamiliar IP by a developer account that normally reads two secrets a week.

corpus-0007.label: malicious
corpus-0007.reason: Instance role credentials should never be used off-instance. Textbook SSRF or metadata-service theft.

corpus-0008.label: benign
corpus-0008.reason: Security team's quarterly access-key audit, run from the corporate network during business hours.

corpus-0009.label: malicious
corpus-0009.reason: Same principal and IP as the Tor recon event, now creating a new admin identity at 4am. Clear attacker persistence step.

corpus-0010.label: benign
corpus-0010.reason: Developer temporarily opened SSH from the office network during a documented incident bridge. Poor practice, not an intrusion.

corpus-0011.label: malicious
corpus-0011.reason: Cross-account grant on a sensitive bucket to an unrecognised account, made late at night from an external address.

corpus-0012.label: benign
corpus-0012.reason: Scheduled key rotation performed by the platform team from the corporate range. Old key deactivated minutes later.

corpus-0013.label: malicious
corpus-0013.reason: Contractor account self-escalating to full admin at 2am from an external IP. No change ticket, no approval.

corpus-0014.label: benign
corpus-0014.reason: Infrastructure-as-code apply expanding a deployment role, run by the usual automation principal from the corporate range in work hours.

corpus-0015.label: malicious
corpus-0015.reason: Mass read of a sensitive bucket at 2am from the same external IP that modified its policy days earlier. Completes the exfiltration chain.

corpus-0016.label: benign
corpus-0016.reason: Monthly analytics backfill job. Runs from a private subnet, same 6am slot every month, reads the same prefix.

corpus-0017.label: malicious
corpus-0017.reason: Snapshotting a volume and making the snapshot public is a well-known exfiltration path with no legitimate use here.

corpus-0018.label: malicious
corpus-0018.reason: Production instance contacting a mining pool. Consistent with post-compromise resource abuse.

corpus-0019.label: benign
corpus-0019.reason: Blockchain research sandbox that legitimately runs mining software. Documented exception, isolated account.

corpus-0020.label: benign
corpus-0020.reason: Continuous internet background noise. Key-only authentication is enforced; no successful logins.

corpus-0021.label: benign
corpus-0021.reason: Untargeted scanning. RDP is restricted to a bastion security group.

corpus-0022.label: malicious
corpus-0022.reason: Sustained, targeted attempts against the bastion specifically, from a single source, followed by a successful authentication.

corpus-0023.label: benign
corpus-0023.reason: Developer travelling; login used MFA and matches their known device and normal working hours in the new timezone.

corpus-0024.label: malicious
corpus-0024.reason: Privileged finance account, no MFA on the session, 2am, unfamiliar geography, immediately followed by permission changes.

corpus-0025.label: malicious
corpus-0025.reason: Disabling audit logging has no legitimate operational purpose here and is a classic anti-forensics step.

corpus-0026.label: benign
corpus-0026.reason: Decommissioning a legacy static-assets bucket. Change ticket exists; performed by automation from the corporate range.

corpus-0027.label: malicious
corpus-0027.reason: Bulk deletion in a production bucket overnight from the same external IP as the finance-admin compromise.

corpus-0028.label: malicious
corpus-0028.reason: C2 beaconing from the same instance later seen mining. Strong indicator of established compromise.

corpus-0029.label: malicious
corpus-0029.reason: DNS tunnelling from an already-compromised host. Completes the compromise chain for this instance.

corpus-0030.label: benign
corpus-0030.reason: Security team's malware analysis sandbox deliberately resolving C2 domains. Isolated VPC, documented exception.

corpus-0031.label: benign
corpus-0031.reason: Bucket intentionally serves a public static website. Change made by automation with an approved ticket.

corpus-0032.label: malicious
corpus-0032.reason: Production bucket holding customer data opened to anonymous read, late at night, from a known-compromised principal's IP.

corpus-0033.label: benign
corpus-0033.reason: Annual billing-settings change that genuinely requires root, performed from the corporate range with MFA during business hours.

corpus-0034.label: malicious
corpus-0034.reason: Root usage at 3am from an unrecognised external IP. Root should never be used this way; treat as full account compromise.

corpus-0035.label: malicious
corpus-0035.reason: Bucket enumeration from the IP already tied to the finance-reports policy change and mass read. Part of the same campaign.

corpus-0036.label: benign
corpus-0036.reason: Security auditor running the scheduled posture assessment from the corporate network. Matches prior monthly runs exactly.

corpus-0037.label: malicious
corpus-0037.reason: Trust-policy enumeration at 3am by the contractor account already seen escalating privileges. Mapping lateral movement paths.

corpus-0038.label: benign
corpus-0038.reason: Build agent pulling a dependency whose mirror is Tor-hosted. Verified against the build log; repeats on every pipeline run.

corpus-0039.label: benign
corpus-0039.reason: Low-reputation score driven by a shared hosting provider. Domain is a legitimate vendor API the application calls constantly.

corpus-0040.label: malicious
corpus-0040.reason: Compromised finance-admin creating a fresh admin identity at 4am. Persistence step following the earlier console compromise.
